title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase with `n` steps. Each move takes you up either 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of different sequences of moves that bring you exactly to the top.
hints: Think about the last move: from which steps could you have arrived at step n?
ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). A plain recursion recomputes the same values exponentially often.
Build up from the bottom, remembering only the previous two counts.

solution.explanation: The final move is either a single or a double step, so ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2), the Fibonacci recurrence. Iterate upward keeping only the last two values. That is O(n) time and O(1) space; naive recursion would take exponential time.
